<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"><p>Sistema capacitivo di messa a terra per RF</p>
<p>Addio al piano di terra!</p>
<table width="488" data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="0" data-align="center" data-border="1" data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td data-valign="top"><img src="schematics/old_symbol.jpg" data-vspace="0" data-hspace="0" data-border="0" width="195" height="278" alt="Rapresentation of what it was thought to be an elementary antenna oscillating circuit " /></td>
<td data-valign="top"><img src="schematics/symbol.jpg" data-vspace="0" data-hspace="0" data-border="0" width="195" height="278" alt="Errante&#39;s true antenna oscillating circuit rapresentation" /></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Come polarizzare correttamente un sistema sbilanciato per segnali a radio-frequenza rispetto alla terra fisica.</p>
<p><strong>Questo sistema dimostra che non � necessario alcun accoppiamento galvanico verso terra per ottenere la corretta messa a terra per segnali elettrici a radio-frequenza.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Sistema capacitivo di messa a terra per RF</strong><br />
<br />
by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p>Faccio seguito a quanto da me rivelato e dimostrato in precedenza in materia di <em>riferimento di terra</em> per i trasduttori radio-elettrici e linee di trasmissione per segnali radio-elettrici. In questa sede rivelo e dimostro che non � necessario alcun accoppiamento galvanico verso terra per ottenere una corretta polarizzazione di un sistema sbilanciato per RF rispetto alla terra fisica.<br />
<br />
TUTTO QUELLO CHE SERVE � una CAPACIT� CONCENTRATA grande abbastanza da esibire una bassissima reattanza capacitiva (&lt;0.5% del valore d'impedenza del radiatore) alla frequenza di lavoro pi� bassa di un dato sistema RF sbilanciato, come mostrato nello schema che segue:</p>
</div>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="1" width="486" height="278" data-cellpadding="0" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" data-valign="top" width="486" height="278"><img src="schematics/capacitive_grounding.jpg" width="486" height="278" alt="Errante&#39;s capacitive RF earth grounding system schematic diagram" /></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<strong>Errante's CAPACITIVE RF EARTH GROUNDING SYSTEM schematic diagram.<br />
An unbalanced radiator and its Un-Un impedance transformer being grounded to the earth by means of a capacitive plate (P) coupled through a dielectric layer to the physical ground - Copyright © 2009 -</strong>
Francesco Errante
<p>�</p>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="1" width="486" height="231" data-cellpadding="0" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="486" height="231"><a href="linee_bilanciate.htm"><img src="schematics/errante_one-wire_transmission_line.jpg" data-vspace="0" data-hspace="0" data-border="0" width="486" height="231" alt="Errante&#39;s capacitive RF earth grounding system applied to the RF transmission line" /></a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<strong>Errante's ONE-WIRE UNBALANCED RF TRANSMISSION LINE, employing Errante's CAPACITIVE RF EARTH GROUNDING SYSTEM - Copyright © 2009 -</strong>
Francesco Errante
<div class="doublespaced">
<p><strong>La <em>capacit� di messa a terra</em></strong> � ottenuta accoppiando un punto di un circuito radio-elettrico che necessita di trovarsi a 0 Volt rispetto a terra, direttamente alla terra fisica per mezzo di un'armatura metallica <strong>(P)</strong> posta su di un piano parallelo ad una superficie uniforme di terra ed isolata dalla stessa da uno strato di materiale dielettrico di adeguate dimenzioni, come mostrato nelle immagini sopra. <strong>(E NON attraverso un condensatore di uguale valore!!! � Anche <em>Guglielmo Marconi</em> e' incorso in questo errore, come documentato nella sua <a href="guglielmo_marconi_premio_nobel.htm#p"><strong>lectio magistralis</strong></a> del 1909 in occasione del suo Premio Nobel)</strong><br />
Nello spettro delle onde medie, lunghe e lunghissime, allo scopo di aumentare la capacit� di messa a terra, l'armatura pu� essere tri-dimenzionale nella forma di un cubo o di un cilindro cavo interrato ma isolato dalla terra. Il volume da esso occupato pu� essere riempito con del calcestruzzo ed usato come fondamenta per torri auto-radianti. Con evidente riduzione dei costi per la realizzazione delle antenne per trasmissioni in VLF per radiodiffusione e militari.<br />
<strong>NB. <span class="small">Il sistema pu� anche essere dotato di percorso galvanico di messa a terra, allo scopo di proteggere gli impianti dai fulmini. Questo percorso pu� essere realizzato mediante un avvolgimento anti-induttivo (RF choke) connesso tra l'armatura (P) ed un'apposita palina di terra.</span></strong><br />
<br />
<strong>L'arrangiamento a semi-condensatore, mostrato negli schemi di cui sopra, NON deve essere confuso per un "<em>piano di terra"</em></strong>. Si comprende facilmente, come per esempio, un'armatura metallica di un metro quadrato circa possa difficilmente fungere da <em>piano di terra</em> in un sistema a 3.5 MHz, mentre risulta molto efficace se ad essere impiegata � la sua reattanza capacitiva. Al contrario, i sistemi di piano di terra a raggiera, ancora in uso, sono di fatto delle rudimentali capacit� distribuite affette da enormi perdite.</p>
<p><strong>Un'applicazione pratica, a dimostrazione di questo sistema, � data� dal <a href="multibanda.htm"><strong><em>SISTEMA MULTIBANDA HF di Errante, con radiatori a 225 Ohm</em></strong></a>�� e suo sistema di alimentazione RF sbilanciato, con messa a terra capacitiva.</strong></p>
</div>

<p><em>VIRTUAL GROUND NODE GENERATOR<br />
for<br />
BALANCED TRANSMISSION LINES</em><br />
<span class="small">in-line "<strong>B</strong>.<strong>V</strong>.<strong>G</strong>.<strong>N</strong>. <strong>G</strong>.", for short</span><br />
<br />
</p>
<p><img src="photos/bal-bal/bvgng_header.jpg" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="580" height="600" alt="Errante&#39;s virtual ground node generator for balanced lines - Errante&#39;s BVGNG" /></p>
<p><em>Virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines</em> .</p>
<p>Freq. range: da 1 a 30 MHz<br />
Input impedance: 300 Ohm<br />
Output impedance: 300 Ohm<br />
Input/output S.W.R.: � 1:1 within freq. range<br />
Insertion loss: -0.01 dB<br />
RF Power: 3 KW cw<br />
Connectors type: M6 studs<br />
Weight : 1 Kg ca.</p>
<p><img src="photos/bal-bal/unbalun_header.jpg" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="580" height="168" alt="Virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines being tested for frequency response flatness within its specified frequency spectrum" /></p>
<p><strong>Picture of the virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines being tested for frequency response flatness.</strong></p>
<p>�</p>
<p><strong>The virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines</strong> : what it is and how it works.</p>
<p><strong>The virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines.</strong><br />
<br />
by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p><strong>The reader who's not already familiar with the virtual ground node mechanism is strongly adviced to read about the <a href="antenna_errante.htm"><em>virtual ground monopole HF antenna</em></a> and its <a href="suppressor.htm">background</a>, prior to proceeding with the reading of this page.</strong><br />
<br />
The virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines and balanced antenna systems (B.V.G.N.G. for short) is a radioelectric circuit based on the same principals governing the <a href="vgng.htm">virtual ground node generator for unbalanced lines</a> and it is built around a broadband high power flux-coupled RF transformer having a 300 Ohm center-tapped balanced primary winding and a 300 Ohm center-tapped balanced secondary winding (Bal-Bal 1:1). The two central-tappings, each of them seat of a virtual ground node, are bonded together and connected to the chassis, ensuring a complete galvanic continuity amongst all the branches of this device.<br />
<br />
This device allows to de-coupling the half-a-wave <a href="balun_300.htm">folded dipole</a> (300 Ohm impedance) from its balanced transmission line (300 Ohm impedance) by imposing a clear-cut electric boundary for the RF signals flowing between the transmission line and the folded dipole antenna, in order for the dipole to exhibit its true bandwidth and for the transmission line not to interfere with it.<br />
In the absence of a clear-cut boundary between the transmission line and the radiator, infact, the transmission line acts as part of the radiating circuit, inevitably, modifying its electrical length and giving it-self origin to <a href="hertzian_radiation.htm">hertzian radiation</a>, with unpleasant consequences such as: loss of signal, radio interferences induction on the surrounding equipment and, above all, the illusion of a phenomenon of resonance of the transmission line it-self. <a href="balanced_lines.htm">Balanced lines</a> are, instead, aperiodic as demonstrated <a href="balanced_lines.htm">here</a>.</p>
<p><img src="photos/bal-bal/dipole_no_line_radiation_low_power.jpg" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="593" height="440" alt="A properly adapted 300 Ohm balanced transmission line terminated on a 1/2 wavelenght folded dipole, through a balanced virtual ground node generator, undergoing a low power radioscopic detection. Experimental verification of the IInd Errante&#39;s law applied to the transmission line" /></p>
<p>A folded dipole and its transmission line, de-coupled through a BVGNG - Radioscopic detection of the RF electric field generated by the radiator and absence of radiation by the balanced transmission line.</p>
<p><img src="photos/bal-bal/dipole_no_line_radiation_high_power.jpg" data-align="center" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="593" height="380" alt="A properly adapted 300 Ohm balanced transmission line terminated on a 1/2 wavelenght folded dipole, through a balanced virtual ground node generator, undergoing an high power radioscopic detection. Experimental verification of the IInd Errante&#39;s law applied to the transmission line" /></p>
<p>A properly adapted 300 Ohm balanced transmission line terminated on a 1/2 wavelenght folded dipole, through a balanced virtual ground node generator, undergoing an high power (1 kW CW) radioscopic detection. Experimental verification of the IInd Errante's law applied to the transmission line</p>
<p><img src="photos/bal-bal/dipole_no_line_radiation_high_power_sideview.jpg" data-align="center" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="593" height="210" alt="A properly adapted 300 Ohm balanced transmission line terminated on a 1/2 wavelenght folded dipole, through a balanced virtual ground node generator, undergoing an high power radioscopic detection. Experimental verification of the IInd Errante&#39;s law applied to the transmission line" /></p>
<p>A properly adapted 300 Ohm balanced transmission line terminated on a 1/2 wavelenght folded dipole, through a balanced virtual ground node generator, undergoing an high power (1 kW CW) radioscopic detection. Experimental verification of the IInd Errante's law applied to the transmission line</p>
<p>This device can be built to suit any impedance transformation ratio. For example: to properly feed an half a wavelength open dipole with a 300 Ohm bifilar transmission line, it is necessary a Bal-Bal having an imput impedance of 300 Ohm ed an output impedance of 70 Ohm.<br />
<br />
<strong>Moreover, the B.V.G.N.G. can be employed to generate a virtual ground node anywhere along a balanced transmission line.</strong></p>
</div>
<p><strong><strong>Scientific relevance:</strong></strong></p>
<table data-border="0" width="400" data-cellpadding="5" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="400"><div class="doublespaced">
<p>The B.V.G.N.G. demonstrates that a balanced transmission line, when correctly de-coupled from the radiator, always exhibits an aperiodic behaviour, even if it is terminated on matched reactive loads.<br />
See: <a href="balanced_lines.htm"><strong>the behaviour of balanced transmission lines for radiofrequency electric signals in a progressive wave regime</strong></a></p>
</div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Operational advantages:</strong></p>
<table data-border="0" width="400" data-cellpadding="5" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="400"><div class="doublespaced">
<p>a) Ensured aperiodicity of the employed balanced transmission line;<br />
<br />
b) inhibition of hertzian radiation onset from the balanced transmission line;<br />
<br />
c) full rejection of the co-phased currents induced onto a balanced transmission lines by any external RF source;<br />
<br />
d) diminuisced signal losses.</p>
</div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<td style="text-align: left;"><p><img src="graphics/new.gif" data-valign="middle" data-border="0" /> <a href="capacitive_grounding.htm">Errante's CAPACITIVE RF EARTH GROUNDING SYSTEM</a></p>
<p>See also: <a href="bvgng.htm">the virtual ground node generator for balanced transmission lines</a></p>
<p>�</p>
<p><span class="small">The</span> <em>in-line VIRTUAL GROUND NODE GENERATOR</em><br />
<span class="small">in-line "<strong>V</strong>.<strong>G</strong>.<strong>N</strong>.<strong>G</strong>.", for short</span><br />
<br />
also known as the<br />
<br />
Errante's Holyground<br />
the network that works miracles!</p>
<p><img src="photos/vgng_header.jpg" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="593" height="396" alt="Errante&#39;s in-line Virtual Ground Node Generator - VGNG" /></p>
<p><em>Errante's in-line virtual ground node generator</em>.<br />
<br />
Freq. range: 1 to 30 MHz<br />
Input imp.: 50 Ohm<br />
Output imp.: 50 Ohm<br />
Input/output SWR: 1:1 within range<br />
Insertion loss: -0.01 dB<br />
RF power: 3 KW cw<br />
Sockets type: SO-239<br />
Weight : 1 Kg ca.<br />
</p>
<p>�</p>
<p><strong>ERRANTE's in-line VIRTUAL GROUND NODE GENERATOR</strong> : what it is, how it works and what it does.</p>
<p><strong>Universal R.F. VIRTUAL GROUND NODE GENERATOR</strong><br />
<br />
by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p>The Errante's in-line virtual ground node generator is a radioelectric circuitry based on the same principals and schematics of his own original patented virtual ground monopole HF antenna design.<br />
<strong>The reader who's not already familiar with the virtual ground node mechanism is strongly adviced to read about the "<a href="antenna_errante.htm"><em>virtual ground monopole HF antenna</em></a> and its <a href="suppressor.htm">background</a> prior to proceeding to the reading of this page.</strong><br />
<br />
The in-line VIRTUAL GROUND NODE GENERATOR (in-line V.G.N.G. for short) is a symmetric radioelectric network which converts an unbalanced RF signal into two precisely identical signals and re-converts them back into a non-inverted single unbalanced RF signal. While doing this, a virtual ground node is generated at its center. It can be effectively described as being an "Un-Bal-Bal-Un" network.<br />
In practice the device, as presented in here, has both the input and output gates terminated onto a 50 Ohm impedance value and SO-239 type of connectors to match the most common co-axial line impedance standard and it is optimized for HF operations between 1 and 30 MHz. Within its specified range, this device appears to be "transparent" between the RF source and the load [SWR = 1:1] and exhibits an extremely low insertion loss [-0.01 dB] However, it can be made to suit any other input/output impedance values and frequencies spectrum.<br />
<br />
<strong>The in-line V.G.N.G. can generate a virtual ground node at any point of a co-axial line in un-balanced transmission line system. This is, infact, its function.</strong> This device is also available in <a href="bvgng.htm">a version for balanced lines</a>.<br />
<br />
<strong>Main applications:</strong><br />
<br />
</p>
</div>
<blockquote>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p><strong>1)</strong> It can be employed to stabilize a whole RTX un-balanced system, however complex it could be, by providing a reliable and centralized RF earth grounding system. As most people may have already experienced, RF earth grounding is a very difficult task and has nothing to do with the conventional safety earth grounding solutions;<br />
<strong><span class="small">N.B. For safety reasons, where required, all the equipment must also be earthed the conventional way and the chassis of the in-line VGNG can also be wired to the building safety earth grounding circuit. All the system equipment chassis should be wired to the provided earth bolts on the in-line VGNG chassis by the shortest route.</span></strong><br />
<br />
<strong>2)</strong> It can be employed to provide a reliable way to short-circuiting antennas who have not antistatic protection, without the need for modifications or even reaching them up on the roof. Since the in-line VGNG exhibits a solid short circuit to the DC current on both its gates, all the electrostatic charges collected by the aerial and/or the co-axial outer conductor will be discharged via common ground and into the building safety earth grounding circuit;</p>
<p><strong>3)</strong> It can be used to stabilize RF co-axial lines exposed to third party hertzian radiation;</p>
<p><strong>4)</strong> It can be employed to stabilize reactive loads at their feeding points.</p>
</div>
</blockquote>
<p><strong>Scientific relevance:</strong></p>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="0" width="400" data-cellpadding="5" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="400"><div class="doublespaced">
<p>The in-line VGNG enables physics and RF laboratories to have a reliable RF earth grounding systems as a precise reference for test and measurement.</p>
</div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Operational advantages:</strong></p>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="0" width="400" data-cellpadding="5" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="400"><div class="doublespaced">
<p>a. the in-line VGNG is easy and fast to deploy;<br />
<br />
b. in-line VGNG helps to improve E.M.I. compatibility within high equipment density environment.</p>
</div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>�</p>
<table width="100%" data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="5" data-border="0">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" data-bgcolor="#FFFF00" width="100%" height="20" data-valign="top"><p><strong>F.A.Q.</strong>:</p>
<p><strong>Question:</strong> I run a virtual ground HF antenna, do I still need an in-line VGNG ?<br />
<strong>ANSWER: NO !</strong> Your virtual ground antenna system already provides all the R.F. earth grounding you need. However, while using a different aerial an in-line VGNG might be needed.</p>
<p><strong>Question:</strong> Where should I place it along my transmission line?<br />
<strong>ANSWER:</strong> Where the un-balanced RTX system comprises only of a TX/RTX-SWRmeter-coaxial-antenna, the in-line VGNG must be placed right onto the TX/RTX antenna socket.<br />
<strong>N.B.</strong> If an antenna tuner is used, the in-line VGNG must always be placed before it, right on its input socket.<br />
If a linear power amplifier is used the in-line VGNG must be placed on its output gate.<br />
Where the system comprises of TX/RTX, a linear power amplifier and an antenna tuner, the in-line VGNG must be placed between the amplifier and the antenna tuner.<br />
If a filter, such as an anti TVI, is used place the filter between the amplifier and the in-line VGNG. Moreover, the filtering should improve and the system will also benefit by the added VGNG's out-of-band own signal rejection.<br />
<strong>N.B.</strong> The in-line VGNG should be inserted in the transmission line by using a short but comfortable RG-213, or better, patch lead. Wherever possible use double male connectors to plug the in-line VGNG in.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<td style="text-align: left;" width="80%" data-valign="top" data-bgcolor="#FFFFFF"><p>Errante's all-in-one hertzian radiation physics apparatus.<br />
<strong>This equipment allows to carry out several measurements and experiments into the physics of radio-electric signals and transducers.</strong></p>
<table data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="5" width="100%" data-border="0">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="100%"><a href="hertzian_radiation.htm"><img src="photos/errante_1st_law.jpg" data-border="0" data-align="center" data-hspace="0" data-vspace="0" width="593" height="442" alt="Energy distribution in a half wave folded dipole and in a half wave open dipole, in a condition of resonance, both fed with RF signals of equal wave lenghth and amplitude" /></a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p><strong>Foreword</strong><br />
<br />
Although more than a century has gone by, since Heinrich Hertz made his first artificial radio transmission, the comprehension of radio-electric phenomena (usually referred to as electromagnetism) has been limited to mere theory. This because, the analysis of radio-electric phenomena had, untill now, relied almost entirely on mathematical conjectures. Mathematics is of great help to physics but cannot take the place of the instrumental observations of the natural phenomena. Instrumental observation is essentially dependant on the progress of technology but, above all, it needs the inventive of scientists without prejudices.<br />
<br />
The apparatus presented here below, allows the step-by-step replication of the main experiments masterminded and made by the <a href="author.htm">author</a> in order to investigate the physics of the radio-electric signals and transducers. These experiments have directly led him into the discovery of the actual mechanism (<em>radio-electric transduction</em>) that originates the hertzian radiation (better known as radio waves). Also read: <a href="hertzian_radiation.htm">Hertzian radiation: what it is and how it happens</a> by <em>Francesco Errante</em><br />
<br />
This equipment enables researchers and teachers alike to carry out several experiments and measurements and makes easy to comprehend how hertzian radiation takes place onto an electric conductor and its propagation in the space. This is done by means of employing gas filled <a href="detector.htm">detector tubes</a> and electric measurements instruments concurrently. This equipment proves it-self to be an invaluable teaching tool, as seeing is believing. It, infact, affords the students a naked eye observation of the energy distribution along both <a href="suppressor.htm">the two branches of the dipole antenna</a> and in its immediate surroundings. Moreover, the electronics that comes with it, permits to vary and to measure the power of the radio-electric signal being injected into the aerial as well as measuring all the relevant standing wave ratios during the signal transduction process, in order to univocally establish causes and effects. (Proportionality between the antenna feeding power and the strength of the generated field; attenuation due to the medium etc...)</p>
</div>

<td style="text-align: center;"><p>SWR-metered BALUN</p>

</p>
<p>This version of the <em>virtual ground balun</em> is designed around our <a href="suppressor.htm">suppressor</a> circuitry and it has 3 built in S.W.R. meters, one for each of its ports. <table data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="5" width="100%" data-border="0">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><p><strong>A VIRTUAL GROUND BALUN FOR DOUBLING THE ï¿½ WAVELENGTH FOLDED DIPOLE ANTENNA</strong></p>
<p>by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<p><strong>Please, pay ATTENTION! This page relates to a special applicazione for scientific purposes of the <em>Errante</em>'s virtual ground balun. To find out more on <em>Errante's</em> virtual ground balun<span class="small">s</span> for HF radio communications and its theory</strong> <a href="balun_errante.htm"><strong>click here</strong></a><strong>.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Scientific purposes</strong></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p><strong>a.</strong> The VIRTUAL GROUND RF BALUN TRANSFORMER described hereby allows the doubling of the ï¿½ wavelength folded dipole's radiator.<br />
<br />
<strong>b.</strong> The virtual ground RF balun transformer described hereby allows to demonstrate that in a ï¿½ wavelength folded dipole antenna, its radiator (having a characteristic impedance of 300 ohm) acts as it was made of two distinct radiators, identical to each other and coinciding with each other, while being fed in a counterphase arrangement, having each of them a characteristic impedance of 150 Ohm, referred to the virtual ground node.<br />
<br />
<strong>c.</strong> The virtual ground RF balun transformer described hereby allows to demonstrate that the ï¿½ wavelength folded dipole radiator and, indeed, any other resonant loop, be it made of any shape, with both a single turn or a multiple turn winding, when it is correctly fed with a sinusoidal radio-electric signal of a proper wavelength, it is always interested by electric currents that flow along its entire length from one end to the other in a clockwise direction for a semi-period and anti-clockwise during the next semi-period or viceversa.</p>
<p><strong>Circuit description</strong><br />
<br />
The Author, by means of a particular <a href="suppressor.htm">radio-electric circuitry</a> for the suppression of any which one of the two branches of a ï¿½ of wavelength open dipole, has previously demonstrated that it is, indeed, possible to feed each of the two branches of an ï¿½ wavelength open dipole independently, so that they can become electrically independent from each other allowing, therefore, to suppress any which one of them without repercussions on the condition of resonance and radiation of the remaining one. On that occasion, the Author has introduced the reader to the concept and the method for generating a virtual ground node for the separation of the dipole's branch currents.<br />
The ï¿½ wavelength folded dipole antenna has a single wiring radiator and, therefore, does not allow the independent usage of the currents flowing on it, both in a clockwise and anti clockwise way.<br />
The present invention allows to split up the folded dipole radiator into two nearly-coinciding wirings in order to demonstrate that the single folded dipole radiator acts as if it was made of two identical but distinct wirings coinciding with each other and each working cyclically for the duration of a semi-period.<br />
This result has been achieved by means of a lumped-constants radio-electric circuit, based around a broad-band flux-coupled radio electric balun transformer(1) winded on a binocular type ferrite core having a primary winding(2) exhibiting an impedance value equal the one of the transmission line(10) being used and a center-tapped secondary winding(3) exhibiting an impedance value of 150 + 150 Ohm.<br />
The said impedance values are referred to the <em>virtual ground</em> node(4 &amp; 6). (a <em>virtual ground node</em> is defined as a point in an electrical circuit that appears to be at ground, but is not actually attached to ground, it is therefore, a node having a 0 degree phase angle difference with respect to ground and has the same electrical potential as the Earth)<br />
The virtual ground node is made available to the whole circuit by means of a very short electrical connection(6) between the transformer center-tapping(4) and the balun chassis(5).<br />
The transformer's working point is optimized by compensation with the employment of high-voltage RF duty capacitors(9).</p>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="1" width="440" height="333" data-cellpadding="0" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="440" height="333"><img src="schematics/balun_300.jpg" width="440" height="333" alt="Errante&#39;s virtual ground balun for doubling the ½ wavelength folded dipole antenna" /></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>It is important to highlight the fact that the two independently fed branches(7 &amp; 8) can also be independently rotated around their common axis to give a variable radiation pattern which ranges from a typical dipole's radiation pattern, if the arms are parallel to each other or a quasi-omnidirectional radiation pattern in the case of the arms being placed perpendicularly to each-other (<a href="quadripole.htm"><strong>turnstile arrangement</strong></a>).</p>
<p><strong>The balun described hereby is characterized by being a <a href="balun_errante.htm"><strong><em>NON fluctuating impedance</em></strong></a> RF electrical transformer. All of its terminations impedance values are set by design, hence the impedance transformation ratio is a function of them and not viceversa, unlike it happens with any other balun arrangement.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Please, pay ATTENTION! This page relates to a special applicazione for scientific purposes of the <em>Errante</em>'s virtual ground balun. To find out more on <em>Errante's</em> virtual ground balun<span class="small">s</span> for HF radio communications and its theory</strong> <a href="balun_errante.htm"><strong>click here</strong></a><strong>.</strong><br />
<br />
</p>
</div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>

Visit <a href="http://www.uibm.gov.it/dati/Titolare.aspx" target="_blank">www.uibm.gov.it</a> and enter <em>Francesco Errante</em> in the search box to see all of my patents, or verify it directly from the <strong><em>European Patent Office</em></strong> archive <a href="http://worldwide.espacenet.com/searchResults?compact=false&amp;ST=advanced&amp;IN=francesco+errante&amp;locale=en_EP&amp;DB=EPODOC&amp;PA=francesco+errante" target="_blank">HERE</a> !</p></td>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td><p><strong>A SECONDARY IONIZATION FLUORESCENCE HERTZIAN RADIATION PASSIVE DETECTOR</strong><br />
<br />
by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p><strong>Description</strong><br />
<br />
"<a href="hertzian_radiation.htm"><em>Hertzian radiation</em></a>" is the oldest, yet the least common way to refer to radio-waves.<br />
The present invention relates to an <em>hertzian radiation</em> passive detector which exploits a secondary ionization fluorescence phenomenon. Untill now, it was thought that the <em>radio-fluorescence</em> phenomenon was only property of very short wavelength emission such as x-ray or those caused by radioactive materials. The detector and its method of employ, as described hereafter, allow to convert an <em>hertzian radiation</em> directly into a visible light radiation so to permit the naked eye appreciation of the <em>hertzian radiation</em>'s energy distribution over the body of a radio antenna, or a <a href="balanced_lines.htm">transmission line</a> and in their immediate surroundings, during transmitting mode. This is, most importantly, done in a non-intrusive manner as the detector is it-self <a href="detector.htm#1">radio-transparent</a> and does not interfere with the resonance and radiation of the radiator. Moreover, the energy absorbed by the detector is neglectable.<br />
As an <em>hertzian radiation</em> invests the low pressure gasses inside the detector, a first ionization takes place with the result that a scattering of higher energy particles will end-up against the luminophore layer covering the inner side of the walls of the detector tube, giving origin to a visible light emission which increases correspondingly to the increase of the flux of the <em>hertzian radiation</em> untill the detector is fully lit.<br />
<br />
In practice, a secondary ionization fluorescence hertzian radiation passive detector in his most elementary and economic form, comprises of a 100 Watt straight fluorescence tube<strong>(1)</strong> for general purpose indoor lighting, having a physical length of about 2.4 meter and a trolley<strong>(2)</strong> which is made of dielectric material and standing on 4 swivel castor wheels.<br />
<br />
The trolley<strong>(2)</strong> allows the detector<strong>(1)</strong> tube to stand up and be free to be moved up and down along the body of the antenna<strong>(3)</strong> under examination, which is placed horizontally and at a suitable height so to encounter the detector at about its middle.<br />
<br />
Generally, a power of little more than 40 Watt RF is enough to fully lit a resonant radiator for the short waves as an � wavelength open dipole antenna. Once the tube is excited, by progressively reducing the RF power supplied to the aerial or by progressively moving the detector away from the radiator, it is possible to visually appreciate the relative strength of the field generated on each and every point along the antenna or its immediate proximity.<br />
<br />
An excited tube will maintain its fluorescence untill the <em>hertzian radiation</em> ceases or drastically diminishes or ceases all together. By reducing the RF power supplied to the exciting antenna, the region of the tube previously lit will decrease correspondingly and its visible light emission will be extinguished as soon as the excitation RF power will drop below 0,1 Watt.<br />
<br />
By means of a number of detector tubes, it is possible to generate a field strength dynamic luminous diagram, both bi-dimensional or tri-dimensional. However, it is advisable to build a diagram by putting together several photograms of the same tube in different point along the radiator. This is easily done by first exciting the tube and then moving it alongside the radiator or the space around the antenna under examination.<br />
Untill the tube is fully lit, to a certain strength of visible radiation correspond a certain strength of the <em>hertzian radiation</em>. It is, therefore, possible to estimate the attenuation introduced by the space in the proximity of the antenna.<br />
<br />
<strong>Scientific purposes</strong><br />
<br />
<strong>a.</strong> The secondary ionization fluorescence hertzian radiation passive detector, as described hereby, allows to demonstrate the <em>hertzian radiation</em>'s transitory ionizing power.<br />
<br />
<strong>b.</strong> The secondary ionization fluorescence hertzian radiation passive detector, as described hereby, allows the naked eye appreciation of the <em>hertzian radiation</em>'s energy distribution over the body of a radio antenna, during transmit mode.<br />
<br />
<strong>c.</strong> The secondary ionization fluorescence hertzian radiation passive detector, as described hereby, allows the naked eye appreciation of the <em>hertzian radiation</em>'s relative intensity and its energy distribution in the space region immediately surrounding the aerial, during transmit mode.<br />
<br />
<strong>d.</strong> The secondary ionization fluorescence hertzian radiation passive detector, as described hereby, allows to see that when a radio-electric signal is injected into a properly resonant radiator, the latter will always radiate energy as radio waves, starting from the point which is always opposite to the point of feeding. The detector, also, shows that the bulk of the energy is always radiated by the region towards the end of the radiator.<br />
<strong>See also:</strong> Hertzian Radiation: what it is and how it happens. <a href="hertzian_radiation.htm">A radioscopic observation</a>, by <em>Francesco Errante</em><br />
<br />
<strong>e.</strong> The secondary ionization fluorescence hertzian radiation passive detector, as described hereby, allows to demonstrate that conventional lighting purpose fluorescent tubes exhibit a much higher energy efficiency and versatility when excited by a radio waves direct bombardment (electrodeless arrangement) as opposed to be exited by galvanic discharge.</p>
</div>

<div class="doublespaced">
<p>The detector is totally radio-transparent untill it lights up. It will become slightly less radio-transparent when fully excited. This however will not affect its performance nor the radiator functioning. In the worst case scenario, when a full intimate parallel coupling between the detector and the end of a radiator is made, a SWR of 1:1,6 would appear when detector lights up.<br />
<br />
</p>

<td style="text-align: left;"><p>Errante's 225 Ohm, multiband HF antenna system.</p>
<p><img src="schematics/16_bands_monopoles.jpg" width="486" height="171" alt="Errante&#39;s 225 Ohm, 16-in-1 multiband HF antenna system, folded monopoles layout " /></p>
<p><img src="schematics/16_bands_dipole.jpg" width="514" height="99" alt="Errante&#39;s 225 Ohm, 16-in-1 multiband HF antenna system, dipole-like center-fed layout" /></p>
<p>Unlocking the full multiband potential of the 225 Ohm elementary radiator in a folded monopole, dipole-like or turnstile layout.</p>
<p><strong>All the I.T.U. amateur radio bands from the 80 m. to the 10 m. band and much more in between, in 16 ample segments.</strong></p>
<p><strong>NB. In order to avoid misunderstandings, it must be noted that this design has nothing to do with the electrically short (&lt;&lt; � lambda) folded monopole, also generically known in this trade as "<em>folded unipole</em>" which is an inherentely lossy and very low impedance radiator.</strong></p>
<table width="594" height="468" data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="0" data-align="center" data-border="1" data-bgcolor="#457090" data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000">

<td><a href="photos/multiband/main_120.jpg"><img src="photos/multiband/main_120_thumb.jpg" data-vspace="0" data-hspace="0" data-border="0" width="308" height="472" alt="Errante&#39;s 2x225 Ohm virtual ground balun for the dipole-like center-fed folded monopoles multiband HF antenna system" /></a></td>
</tr>

</table>
<p><span class="small">click on the images to enlarge them</span></p>
<p><strong>Errante's 2x225 Ohm virtual ground balun for the dipole-like center-fed folded monopoles multiband HF antenna system.<br />
Notice the two pivoting UV resistant Nylon insulators - each of them 42 cm long - which make easy the anchoring of 2 folded monopoles on each side of the balun. This is an ideal solution to install all the dipole branches with any angle from about 120 degree to 180 and upwards again to the 120 degree. From inverted "Vee" to open dipole and up to a "V".<br />
The insulators are free to rotate around their axis, being the M8 studs which also act as the balun's electrical terminals.<br />
The insulators and the eyelet terminals are tightened independently from each other.</strong></p>
<p>�</p>
<p>Errante's 225 Ohm, multiband HF antenna system: what it is and how it works.</p>
<p>by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p>The multiband radio-electric transducer system disclosed hereby is based upon the natural <em>harmonic resonance</em>, a very well known physics phenomenon. This system, therefore, does not utilize traps or loading coils or other artifacts for band segmentation.<br />
<br />
The radiators act, band by band, as mono-band full-size aerials by resonating on a different fraction or a multiple of the relevant signal wavelength, starting from 3/4 a wavelength at each set lowest operating band.<br />
<br />
By virtue of this radiator design, it possible to get several, well distinct, sets of bands, each set giving 8 bands in the spectrum of the HF, each and all of them yelding a COMMON IMPEDANCE VALUE of 225 Ohm. <strong>This particular common impedance value is the key factor in this system design</strong>, while <em>Radiondistics' own patented virtual ground broadband impedance coupling and phasing network technology</em> has allowed this system to work seamlessly with an exceptional impedance matching throughout all its frequency ranges. <strong>NO additional A.T.U. (antenna tuning unit) is needed and all its operating bands offer a generous width as this is an high impedance antenna system.</strong><br />
<br />
Moreover, this system requires only a reasonable amount of space to be deployed, it is easy to install and does not require tedious adjustment of the length of its radiators, as all of its bands are well defined but NOT critical. If necessary, the radiator can even be bent along its axis (this will definitely affect its radiation pattern but not its original tuning) or installed as a top fed sloper or as a center-fed inverted-vee with any angle with respect to the ground. It also requires very little room clearance from the ground or any other surrounding obstacles. Thanks to the <em>Radiondistics' proprietary RF feeding system</em>, no de-tuning takes place on the aerials unless they are almost right down onto the ground. <strong>For example, a 225 Ohm folded monopole arrangement, for all the I.T.U. amateur radio bands, from the 80 meter to the 10 meter, plus a lot more in between, would take about 26.5 meters of space on a streight line, while a center-fed dipole-like arrangement would need just twice as much</strong>.</p>
<p>Accordingly, a range of feeding systems have been deviced for:<br />
<br />
<strong>folded monopole antennas with <a href="capacitive_grounding.htm"><strong>Errante's capacitive earth grounding</strong></a> ;<br />
<br />
<strong>center-fed dipole-like antennas. See <a href="balun_errante.htm"><strong>Errante's 50/225+225 Ohm balun</strong></a> ;<br />
<br />
<strong>folded monopole antennas with <a href="antenna_errante.htm"><strong>Errante's virtual grounding</strong></a> ;<br />
<br />
<strong>folded monopoles in a <a href="quadripole.htm"><strong>turnstile antenna configuration</strong></a>.</strong></strong></strong></strong><br />
<br />
</p>
</div>

<table data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="5" width="100%" data-border="0">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><p><strong>ERRANTE's BALUN</strong> : what it is, how it works and how it came to be made.</p>
<p>by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p>The virtual ground balun presented hereby is the practical application in the field of the short wave radio communications of what the Author has previously created for scientific purposes. It, infact, along with the <a href="balun_300.htm">virtual ground balun for doubling the � wavelength folded dipole antenna</a>, descends from the <a href="suppressor.htm"><strong>radio-electric circuitry for the suppression of anyone of the two branches of a � of wavelength open dipole</strong></a>.<br />
<br />
<em>Errante's</em> balun is, essentially, a pure electrical transformer which, in its most elementary layout, has a minimum of 3 tuned circuits: a primary circuit (primary winding LC network) and 2 secondary circuits (secondary windings LC networks).<br />
Generally, the <em>Errante's</em> balun secondary circuits are identical to each other in order to feed symmetrical balanced antennas. When necessary, the secondary windings can be formed to have impedance values different between each other, while maintaining the phase angle difference of the balanced terminations to a constant �90 degree with respect to the virtual ground node. Moreover, as all the pure electrical transformers, <em>Errante's</em> balun can be made to have more than a couple of secondary windings.<br />
<br />
<strong><em>Errante's</em> balun is characterized for NON allowing any impedance transformation to take place unless its terminations impedance values are matched (NON-fluctuating impedance).<br />
<em>Errante's</em> balun terminations impedance values are set by design, hence the impedance transformation ratio is a function of them and not viceversa, unlike it happens with any other balun arrangement.</strong> See for example the <a href="#1"><em>Guanella's</em> or the <em>Ruthroff's</em> transformers</a> which are instead characterized by having a fluctuating terminations impedance values, as they are nothing else than an arrangement of auto-transformers, their input and output circuits are unseparable and, therefore, any change made to their primary circuits will inevitably affect their secondary circuits.<br />
In practice, a balun having a fluctuating termination impedance value carries out its impedance transformation duty within a very ample range of impedance values, changing its input termination impedance according to the one of its load and viceversa. Therefore, supposed we have a <em>Guanella's</em> type balun with a transformation ratio of 4:1, it will show an input impedance of 75 Ohm if its load impedance is of 300 Ohm, or it will show an input impedance of 50 Ohm if its load impedance is of 200 Ohm. <strong>This cannot happen if an <em>Errante's</em> type of balun is employed, because each termination impedance value is a fixed property of the relevant termination and does not vary even if there is a change in the values of the impedance of the circuits (antennas or transmission lines) connected to them.<br />
By limiting the line-load system impedance to the imposed values only, it is possible to inhibit both lines and loads (antennas) from giving origins to unwanted resonances, which are, generally, harmonic resonances, very often deriving from the presence of more than a load on the same feed-point, which generates alternative paths for the RF.</strong> (for example: multiple dipoles o monopoles, fan antennas and so on). <strong>This is something not to be underestimated, not only with regard to the transmitting phase but and above all, to the receiving phase as well. Employing a NON-fluctuating impedance balun, infact, introduces a very high rejection to interfering radio signals from sources outside the bands of the radio spectrum for which an antenna is ment. This translates in an excellent stability and selectivity of the transmission line or antenna systems which employ <em>Errante's</em> baluns.</strong><br />
<br />
A virtual ground balun represents the ideal device for the correct feeding of dipole and loop antennas. The virtual ground balun carries out many functions at once allowing to:<br />
1) match the RF source impedance to the chosen load while introducing neglectable insertion loss of power;<br />
2) transform the RF signal fed to it into two identical portions with the correct phase angle difference for the natural feeding of open or folded dipoles and loop antennas;<br />
3) obtain a virtual ground node for the correct polarization of its unbalanced port;<br />
4) obtain a common ground path for the dissipation of the charges induced by the electrostatic phenomena;<br />
5) obtain an high de-coupling between its two balanced ports.<br />
<br />
The generic virtual ground balun's schematic diagram is shown here below.</p>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="1" width="440" data-cellpadding="0" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="440" height="222"><img src="schematics/balun_main.jpg" width="440" height="320" alt="VIRTUAL GROUND BALUN - Errante&#39;s balun" /></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>The virtual ground balun is housed inside a weatherproof rugged metal enclosure having two separate compartments: one hosts the balun circuitry while the other one protects the coaxial connectors. The said metal enclosure not only ensures an high mechanical robustness and a total stability against the weather agents, it also works as the general electric conductor for all the references to the virtual ground node. Such an enclosure ensures also a full electrostatic shielding of the RF balun transformer circuitry.<br />
<br />
<em>Radiondistics</em> claims the originality of the balun's unique electromechanical layout, as well as the balun radio-electric circuitry.</p>
<p><strong>Operational advantages:</strong></p>
<table data-bordercolor="#000000" data-bordercolorlight="#000000" data-bordercolordark="#000000" data-border="0" width="400" data-cellpadding="5" data-cellspacing="0" data-align="center">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="400"><p>a. the virtual ground balun allows the feeding of dipole and loop antennas with much less loss than conventional baluns<br />
<br />
b. the virtual ground balun allows an aerial to exhibit a much larger bandwidth compared to when the same antenna is fed by a conventional balun.<br />
<br />
c. the virtual ground balun allows an antenna to exhibit a much stronger immunity to parasitic capacitive effects compared to when the same antenna is fed by conventional baluns.<br />
<br />
d. the virtual ground balun allows an antenna to exhibit a strong resonance stability, regardless of the level and inclination of it above the ground.<br />
<br />
e. the virtual ground balun allows an antenna to exhibit a much stronger immunity to out-of-band emissions compared to when the same aerial is fed by a conventional balun.<br />
<br />
f. the virtual ground balun allows an antenna to exhibit a much stronger immunity to electrostatic charges and noises compared to when it is fed by a conventional balun.<br />
<br />
g. the virtual ground balun, owing to the constructive and destructive interference phenomena taking place in the transformer allows the dipole antenna to exhibit a sharper radiation/reception pattern (off the beam axis signal rejection) compared to the same aerial when fed by a conventional balun.<br />
<br />
h. the virtual ground balun allows a much faster antenna deployment time compared to conventional baluns.<br />
<br />
i. the virtual ground balun allows an antenna to exhibit a much better compatibility with highly populated environments (EMC TVI) compared to when it is fed by a conventional baluns.</p></td>
</tr>

</table>

<td style="text-align: left;"><p>�</p>
<p><strong>ERRANTE's HF Turnstile antenna broadband driver</strong> : what it is, how it works and what it does.</p>
<p>by <em>Francesco Errante</em></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p>The Errante's turnstile antenna driver, is a broadband radioelectric circuit based on our own original <a href="balun_errante.htm"><em>virtual ground balun</em></a> patented design.<br />
A <em>turnstile antenna</em>, which is also known as <em>cross-dipole or quadripole</em> is the top choice when a quasi-omnidirectional radiation pattern is requided in a horizontally polarized antenna system. � (<a href="pdf/turnstile_antenna_patent.pdf" target="_blank">see the 1937, George H. Brown's original patent application</a>)<br />
When it comes to point to point and broadcast radiocommunications through the ionospheric radio-propagation, such systems have the advantage of following the wanted signals, no matter what changes in the direction of propagation the sky makes.<br />
Trans-ionospheric effects include refraction, amplitude and phase scintillation, signal delay and polarisation rotation. Such changes always affect the strength of the wanted signal during ionospheric radio propagation reception (fading, evanescence, QSB) and can easily reach a 20 dB loss. <strong>A turnstile antenna system driven by this device of ours will recover that loss and on average all signals are 10 to 15 dB higher compared to what a single dipole would extract in the same conditions</strong>.<br />
Untill now, making a proper turnstile antenna for the short wave bands used to be a mammuth task and no previous system could allow multiband operation owing to their own delay line limitation.<br />
The device presented hereby is, instead, the ideal solutions to manage a cross dipole as you would do with a single one. It, infact, exhibits the same properties as our own virtual ground balun, while making easy to drive 2 identical dipoles or 2 identical fan dipoles in a <em>turnstile configuration</em>, thanks to its unique phasing system. By eliminating the need for a delay line, our system also eliminates all the loss of signal that inevitably comes with it, therefore, the quantity of energy tranferred to each of the 2 dipoles is precisely the same, this will translate in a truly symmetrical radiation patten.<br />
Where fan-dipoles cannot be used through lack of space, multiband operations can also be achived by employing trapped dipole branches. <strong>NOW, also available in the Errante's 225 Ohm, multiband monopoles version. (<a href="multiband.htm"><strong>Errante's 225 Ohm, multiband HF antenna system</strong></a>)</strong></p>
<p><strong>The turnstile antenna system, as presented hereby, it's the top choice for digital communications over the HF spectrum, such as the <em>e-mail over the HF services</em> and the like.</strong><br />
<br />
</p>
</div></td>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="600" height="60"><h1 id="energy-and-radiation-wavelength">Energy and radiation wavelength</h1>
<p><strong>NB</strong>: this page is an appendix to the<br />
<a href="hertzian_radiation.htm"><em>Errante's</em> hertzian radiation theorem.</a></p>
<p><a href="hertzian_radiation.htm"><strong>Understanding radiowaves.</strong><br />
The radio-electric transduction phenomenon originating the hertzian radiation, as discovered by this author.</a></p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="600" height="40"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;" width="100%" height="30" data-valign="top" data-bgcolor="#FFFFFF"><p><img src="graphics/new.gif" data-valign="middle" data-align="center" data-border="0" />  <a href="rf_lighting_devices/index.html" target="_top">Hertzian radiation as a convenient means for artificial lighting source.</a><br />
<br />
<img src="graphics/new.gif" data-valign="middle" data-align="center" data-border="0" />   <a href="hertzian_radiation.htm">Hertzian radiation and the <em>Hallwachs-effect</em>, better known as the <em>photovoltaic effect</em>.</a><br />
<br />
<img src="graphics/new.gif" data-valign="middle" data-align="center" data-border="0" />   <a href="hertzian_radiation.htm">Hertzian radiation studies deliver a major blow to the<br />

<table width="600" data-cellspacing="0" data-cellpadding="0" data-border="0">

<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;" width="600" height="200" data-valign="top" data-bgcolor="#FFFFFF"><h3 id="frequency-wavelength-energy-calculator">Frequency / Wavelength / Energy Calculator</h3>
<p><br />
Frequency and wavelength of radiations are related to one another through the speed at which light travels.<br />
<br />
Equation: f * λ = c<br />
Equation: E = <sup>hc</sup>/<sub>λ</sub><br />
<br />
where:<br />
f = frequency in Hertz (Hz = <sup>1 cycle</sup>/<sub>sec</sub>)<br />
λ = wavelength in meters (m)<br />
c = the speed of light (approximately equal to 3*10<sup>8</sup> <sup>m</sup>/<sub>s</sub>)<br />
E = energy in electron Volts (eV)<br />
h = Planck's constant (6.626068 × 10<sup>-34</sup> <sup>m<sup>2</sup>kg</sup>/<sub>s</sub>)<br />
<br />
</p>
<p>To convert wavelength to frequency enter the wavelength in microns (μm) and press "Calculate f and E". The corresponding frequency will be in the "frequency" field in GHz.<br />
<br />
OR enter the frequency in gigahertz (GHz) and press "Calculate λ and E" to convert to wavelength.<br />
Wavelength will be in μm.<br />
<br />
OR enter the energy in eV and click "Calculate λ and F" and the values will appear in the corresponding fields.</p>
<p> </p></td>
</tr>

&#10;<h3 id="complete-list-of-frequency-wavelength-units-for-conversion">Complete list of frequency wavelength units for conversion</h3>
<ul>
<li>hertz [Hz]</li>
<li>1 exahertz [EHz] = 1.0E+18 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/exahertz-to-hertz.htm">exahertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-exahertz.htm">hertz to exahertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 petahertz [PHz] = 1.0E+15 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/petahertz-to-hertz.htm">petahertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-petahertz.htm">hertz to petahertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 terahertz [THz] = 1000000000000 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/terahertz-to-hertz.htm">terahertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-terahertz.htm">hertz to terahertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 gigahertz [GHz] = 1000000000 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/gigahertz-to-hertz.htm">gigahertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-gigahertz.htm">hertz to gigahertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 megahertz [MHz] = 1000000 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/megahertz-to-hertz.htm">megahertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-megahertz.htm">hertz to megahertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 kilohertz [kHz] = 1000 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/kilohertz-to-hertz.htm">kilohertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-kilohertz.htm">hertz to kilohertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 hectohertz [hHz] = 100 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/hectohertz-to-hertz.htm">hectohertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-hectohertz.htm">hertz to hectohertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 dekahertz [daHz] = 10 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/dekahertz-to-hertz.htm">dekahertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-dekahertz.htm">hertz to dekahertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 decihertz [dHz] = 0.1 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/decihertz-to-hertz.htm">decihertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-decihertz.htm">hertz to decihertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 centihertz [cHz] = 0.01 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/centihertz-to-hertz.htm">centihertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-centihertz.htm">hertz to centihertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 millihertz [mHz] = 0.001 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/millihertz-to-hertz.htm">millihertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-millihertz.htm">hertz to millihertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 microhertz [µHz] = 1.0E-6 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/microhertz-to-hertz.htm">microhertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-microhertz.htm">hertz to microhertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 nanohertz [nHz] = 1.0E-9 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/nanohertz-to-hertz.htm">nanohertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-nanohertz.htm">hertz to nanohertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 picohertz [pHz] = 1.0E-12 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/picohertz-to-hertz.htm">picohertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-picohertz.htm">hertz to picohertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 femtohertz [fHz] = 1.0E-15 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/femtohertz-to-hertz.htm">femtohertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-femtohertz.htm">hertz to femtohertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 attohertz [aHz] = 1.0E-18 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/attohertz-to-hertz.htm">attohertz to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-attohertz.htm">hertz to attohertz</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 cycle/second = 1 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/cycle-second-to-hertz.htm">cycle/second to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-cycle-second.htm">hertz to cycle/second</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 wavelength in exametres = 2.99792458E-10 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/wavelength-in-exametres-to-hertz.htm">wavelength in exametres to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-wavelength-in-exametres.htm">hertz to wavelength in exametres</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 wavelength in petametres = 2.99792458E-7 hertz [Hz]
<div>
<a href="/frequency-wavelength/wavelength-in-petametres-to-hertz.htm">wavelength in petametres to hertz</a>,   <a href="/frequency-wavelength/hertz-to-wavelength-in-petametres.htm">hertz to wavelength in petametres</a>
</div></li>
<li>1 wavelength in terametres = 0.0002997925 hertz [Hz]
<div>

<p><strong>Descrizione</strong></p>
<div class="doublespaced">
<p>La "<a href="radiazione_hertziana.htm"><em>radiazione hertziana</em></a>" � uno dei modi meno in voga, ma pi� antichi per riferirsi alle emissioni nello spettro delle radio-onde. La presente invenzione concerne un rivelatore passivo a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria, intrinsecamente non-invasivo, a bombardamento diretto, per radiazioni hertziane, capace di convertire la radiazione hertziana in radiazione luminosa nello spettro del visibile, consentendo l'apprezzamento visivo della distribuzione energetica sul corpo di un'antenna radio o su di una <a href="linee_bilanciate.htm">linea di trasmissione</a> e nello spazio in loro prossimit� durante la sua trasmissione di segnali radioelettrici nello spazio. Il rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana qui presentato permette di essere posto a contatto dell'antenna od nella sua immediata prossimit� senza che lo stesso ne disturbi il suo comportamento, grazie al fatto che esso � <a href="detector_it.htm#1">radio-trasparente</a>. Esso produce un'emissione luminosa nello spettro del visibile, dovuta a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria provocata dalla radiazione hertziana sui gas presenti all'interno del tubo rivelatore stesso. La sua emissione luminosa cresce al crescere dell'intensit� del flusso della radiazione che lo investe.<br />
Un rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana nel suo allestimento pi� elementare e pi� economico, consiste di un tubo fluorescente(1) ai vapori di mercurio, del tipo per illuminazione ambientale da 100W, della lunghezza di 2,4 metri ed un carrello su ruote(2), costruito con materiale dielettrico che permette al tubo rivelatore(1) di essere mantenuto in posizione verticale e di poter scorrere lungo il corpo dell'antenna radio(3) sotto esame, posta orizzontalmente rispetto al suolo ed ad un livello tale da incontrare il tubo rivelatore, pressappoco in coincidenza del centro dell'altezza di quest'ultimo.<br />
In genere, � sufficiente una potenza di poco superiore ai 40 Watt RF, perch� un radiatore risonante per onde corte come un dipolo aperto a � onda, inneschi la fluorescenza in tutto il tubo. Il tubo rivelatore una volta innescato permette, riducendo progressivamente la potenza fornita al radiatore sotto esame o scostando lo stesso dall'antenna, di apprezzare visivamente l'intensit� del campo prodotto dall'antenna in ogni suo punto e nello spazio in sua stretta prossimit�. Una volta innescato, il tubo rivelatore continuer� a mantenere la sua fluorescenza fino al cessare od al diminuire drasticamente della radiazione hertziana. Riducendo progressivamente la potenza di alimentazione dell'antenna eccitatrice(3), si riduce corrispondentemente anche la lunghezza della regione di tubo rivelatore illuminata e la sua emissione luminosa si estingue non appena la potenza di eccitazione scende al di sotto di 0,1 Watt circa.<br />
Con l'uso di pi� tubi rivelatori, � possibile creare un diagramma luminoso dinamico, bidimensionale o tridimensionale, dell'intensit� del campo irradiato dall'antenna, ma � consigliabile invece costruire il diagramma attraverso il montaggio di pi� fotogrammi dello stesso tubo su vari punti dell'antenna. Ci� � facilmente realizzabile facendo scorrere il tubo, una volta innescato, su vari punti dell'antenna in esame o dello spazio nell'immediata prossimit� dell'antenna in esame. Fino al raggiungimento della saturazione luminosa del tubo, ad uguale intensit� della radiazione luminosa da esso emessa, corrisponde uguale intensit� della radiazione hertziana che ne sostiene l'eccitazione a quel livello. E'possibile, pertanto, stimare anche l'attenuazione della radiazione hertziana introdotta dallo spazio in stretta prossimit� dell'antenna.<br />
<br />
E' stato cos� inventato un rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria che permette di compiere indagini visive dirette sul comportamento delle antenne radio e delle radiazioni da esse generate tramite lo sfruttamento del <strong>potere ionizzante delle radio-onde, qui implicitamente dimostrato</strong>.<br />
<br />
<br />
<strong>Funzioni scientifiche</strong><br />
<br />
<strong>a.</strong> Il rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria qui descritto consente di dimostrare il potere ionizzante transitorio della radiazione hertziana.<br />
<br />
<strong>b.</strong> Il rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria qui descritto consente di apprezzare ad occhio nudo la distribuzione energetica della radiazione hertziana in un'antenna radio in fase di trasmissione.<br />
<br />
<strong>c.</strong> Il rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria qui descritto consente di apprezzare ad occhio nudo l'intensit� relativa e la distribuzione energetica di una radiazione hertziana nella regione di spazio immediatamente circostante un'antenna radio in fase di trasmissione.<br />
<br />
<strong>d.</strong> Il rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria qui descritto consente di vedere che � sempre la parte terminale di un radiatore, ovvero quella opposta al punto di alimentazione, ad essere responsabile per la gran parte della radiazione hertziana da esso emessa. La distribuzione energetica della radiazione all'atto della fuoriuscita dal radiatore NON � sinusoidale. E' ragionevole ipotizzare che il corpo del radiatore stesso funga da rampa per gran parte della sua lunghezza e che la radiazione avvenga soltanto alla sua estremita', ove le cariche elettriche non potendo pi� avanzare ritornano in dietro per scontrarsi con un nuovo fronte d'onda proveniente dal punto di alimentazione del radiatore stesso. Non � possibile ammettere che lo <em>scattering</em> avvenga soltanto perche' le cariche non possano pi� proseguire nel loro percorso una volta raggiunta la fine del conduttore e ci� perch�, altrimenti, non si avrebbe il fenomeno della risonanza. Ne deriva che la risonanza puo' concepirsi come un regime para-stazionario o controllato.<br />
<strong>Leggi anche:</strong> La Radiazione Hertziana: <a href="radiazione_hertziana.htm">un'osservazione radioscopica</a>, di <em>Francesco Errante</em><br />
<br />
<strong>e.</strong> Il rivelatore passivo di radiazione hertziana a fluorescenza da ionizzazione secondaria qui descritto consente di dimostrare come i segnali radioelettrici impiegati nell'eccitazione per bombardamento diretto di tubi fluorescenti convenzionali per illuminazione, permettano agli stessi un'efficienza e versatilit� di molto superiore al metodo tradizionale di eccitazione per attraversamento galvanico da corrente alternata a bassa frequenza.</p>
</div>
